subject: Litmus security: supply-chain coverage & phased evidence handoff
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@litmus.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: security@litmus.ai, procurement@litmus.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Litmus: request for subprocessor coverage + materials for SOC 2 / SIG review

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — Litmus is running a SIG + SOC 2 intake for our cloud procurement review and we need a clear subprocessor roster and mapped evidence for a handful of controls (data residency, KMS ownership, SOC2 report availability, and incident response delegation).

Specifically can you provide: 
- A current subprocessor roster with residency, purpose, and whether they have access to customer data (yes/no)
- Any SOC 2 or SIG artifacts that map to subprocessors (attestations, CAIQ sections, or redacted reports)
- A short note on how KMS keys are assigned/rotated and whether any subprocessors hold keys or key material

We'd like to get the roster and evidence index by EOD Wednesday (2025-09-24) so procurement can greenlight the contract path. If you can suggest a phased delivery (minimal CSV + index first, then artifact bundles), that would help.

Appreciate it — cc'ing our procurement contact.

Best,
Anika Rao
Security Program Manager
Litmus AI

--
[External] Please consider the environment before printing this email.

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@litmus.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Litmus: request for subprocessor coverage + materials for SOC 2 / SIG review

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely support this and will deliver in a phased manner to meet your procurement timeline. Plan below (aiming to have phase 1 to you tomorrow EOD):

Phase 1 (tomorrow EOD) — roster + index
- subprocessor_roster_20250922.csv: vendor, role, country, data access (yes/no), scope note
- evidence_index_20250922.pdf: one-page index that maps roster rows to artifacts (SOC 2 sections, SIG control IDs, CAIQ categories)

Phase 2 (by Fri 2025-09-26) — artifact bundles
- Redacted SOC 2 report (PDF): available for customers under NDA; we'll provide a redacted copy through our secure drive link
- CAIQ mapping extract and SIG evidence snippets (PDF)
- kms-residency-matrix.xlsx: key owners, residency, and whether key material leaves Redwood infrastructure

Notes / clarifications needed from Litmus:
1) Confirm whether you need full document-level redaction or just PII removal for the SOC 2 report. We typically provide redacted reports for procurement (redactions applied to customer names and internal-only IP).
2) For KMS: do you want a high-level diagram or a full account-level mapping? We can provide both; the full mapping will take longer and needs a data-handling agreement addendum if you require account-level principals.
3) Any additional compliance frameworks to map (e.g., HIPAA, if you're handling PHI)?

Attachments for phase 1 are included with this email. If you want to start with a quick 20-minute call to align expectations, I'm free tomorrow 11:00–12:00 and 15:00–16:30 PT.

Olga Petrov
Senior Trust & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: subprocessor_roster_20250922.csv (text/csv)]
[attachment: evidence_index_20250922.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Litmus - evidence packaging and KMS wording for procurement

Olga / Jonas — quick internal note to confirm next steps now that I uploaded the phase-1 files to the secure drive (link below) and prepped the redaction template for SOC 2. Key points: 

- I added a short "artifactConfidence" column in the roster to indicate whether we can provide full docs ("full"), redacted ("redacted"), or snippet ("snippet"). Helps procurement triage.
- For KMS language, recommend we provide the following summary in the evidence index: 
  "Redwood Inference retains control of customer encryption keys. Keys are generated and stored in customer-scoped KMS instances. Subprocessors do not hold private key material; where third-party managed services are used, we disclose the provider and residency in the kms-residency-matrix.xlsx."
  This avoids leaking account-level principals while being explicit on custody.
- Jonas: please confirm legal is OK with the standard redaction (remove customer names & contract numbers, leave control descriptions). If they want a different approach, flag ASAP.

Drive link (phase 1 uploads): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/LITMUS-Subproc-Evidence-20250922

I also attached the preliminary KMS matrix to this thread so we can iterate before sending to Litmus.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Trust
Redwood Inference
[attachment: kms-residency-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Anika Rao <anika@litmus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: security@litmus.ai, procurement@litmus.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Litmus: request for subprocessor coverage + materials for SOC 2 / SIG review

Hi Olga / Marissa — thanks, this is perfect. We received the roster + index in the drive and procurement confirms the phased approach works. A few requests before we close the intake: 

- Please proceed with the standard SOC 2 redaction template you mentioned (customer names & contract numbers redacted).
- For KMS: the summary paragraph you suggested is sufficient for procurement; we do not need account-level mapping. Please include a short note that rotation schedules follow our standard cryptographic hygiene (rotate keys at least annually; emergency rotation policies are documented).
- Can you add a short row in the roster for any ephemeral control-plane providers (e.g., telemetry services) even if they do not access plaintext customer data? Procurement wants full visibility.

We may follow up with a brief clarification later, but this looks good. I'll share the drive link with our risk team.

Best,
Anika Rao
Security Program Manager
Litmus AI
